author: Inside Edition
description: FBI agents are canvassing gun stores in the Tucson area with a list of names and photos of potential suspects in Nancy Guthrie's kidnapping. Authorities are looking for someone who bought the gun seen in the surveillance video at Guthrie's front door. The photos and names were apparently obtained by searching through Walmart's sales records for whoever bought the backpack the suspect wore. Meanwhile, DNA samples found in Guthrie's home and in a discarded glove are being run through commercial databases.
title: FBI Agents Canvas Gun Stores In Nancy Guthrie Kidnapping Investigation

author: Inside Edition
description: After a frantic search for nine daredevil skiers feared buried by an avalanche in the High Sierras, eight have been found dead by rescuers. One skier remains missing. The skiers were on a 3-day back-country adventure when a fierce blizzard hit. Controversy is erupting as some are questioning why they were out during a blizzard. A mountain rescue training team in Utah demonstrated to Inside Edition in 2012 how a backpack airbag might work in an emergency.
title: 8 Of 9 Missing Skiers After Avalanche Found Dead

author: Inside Edition
description: Authorities say they have had it with the army of YouTubers streamers camped out in front of Nancy Guthrie's home. True crime influencers from across the nation stream for hours to thousands of followers. Jimmy Williams sits all day in a lawn chair, streaming around the clock. Arizona State Rep. Alma Hernandez  said if streamers truly want to be helpful "they should probably go home." YouTube streamer Damian Enderly says his audience is hungry for coverage of the case.
title: Authorities Want YouTube Streamers Outside Guthrie Home To Leave

author: Inside Edition
description: Video shows a child plummeting from a zipline. Knox was celebrating his 10th birthday at an indoor adventure park. Knox, wearing a full body harness, plunged over 20 feet to the floor below. Knox suffered a concussion but is expected to make a full recovery. The incident occurred at Spy Ninjas HQ. The company tells Inside Edition the safety of their guests is a priority and their staff gave Knox prompt medical attention. They also say the zip line was inspected and declared safe by an independent inspector after the incident and is now reopened.
title: 10-Year-Old Boy Plummets 20 Feet From Zipline

author: Inside Edition
description: Video shows the moment police confronted Kris Harrison, who was accused of shooting and killing his daughter after a heated argument over President Donald Trump. His 23-year-old daughter Lucy was visiting Texas from England. Reporters say the two clashed over the dad's conservative politics. When police arrived, bodycam footage shows the dad explaining Lucy was headed back to England when the fatal shooting happened. He says it was accidental. A grand jury decided not to file charges.
title: Did This Father Kill His Daughter Over Argument About President Trump?

author: Inside Edition
description: An open casting call was held Wednesday in the search for the next Pamela Anderson and other "Baywatch" characters. Despite the cold weather, hundreds of hopefuls appeared in swimwear to show off their best "Baywatch" poses. "Baywatch" debuted in 1989 and became the most-watched show in the world, reaching more than one billion viewers every week. The reboot is expected to come out later this year.
title: Hundreds Of Hopefuls Attend 'Baywatch' Reboot Open Casting Call

author: Inside Edition
description: It was a true house of horrors for dozens of animals that were allegedly being hoarded at this house in Michigan. The Flint Township Police released video of the rescue where it says 61 dogs and three cats were found living in squalor. Rescuers say the air was toxic with ammonia at hazardous levels. They had to work in shifts to recover the animals who were all suffering from the effects of living in such unsanitary conditions. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: 61 Dogs, 3 Cats Rescued From Hoarding House In Michigan

author: Inside Edition
description: Some job listings are about making money, but not for the person applying for work. Bonnie Haring of Pennsylvania says a scammer got a lot of her money after she answered an ad for a remote job. She tells CBS News the position involved approving positive hotel reviews, but she says they required her to pay $100 of her own money, and the charges kept on coming. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Woman Loses $220G In Scam After Applying For Remote Job

author: Inside Edition
description: Matthew Miller first met the sea lion pup when he was out on his boat with his daughter in San Clemente.
title: Sea Lion Pup 'Asks' Human Family For Help #shorts

description: Inside Edition accompanied former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star Brandi Glanville on the day of her life-saving surgery.
title: Inside Look At Brandi Glanville's Life-Saving Surgery #shorts
